observed_reviews.body:
Independent check of the retained `discovery/MODEL.mps.gz` at head `be656882`. I tried to turn the numerical `kOptimal` into an exact certificate. Result: **a rigorous ceiling, but not an optimality proof.**

**Setup.** I parsed the MPS with my own reader, keeping every coefficient as an exact decimal fraction: 9,276 binary columns, 5,263 equality rows and 4,169 ≤ rows. HiGHS 1.15.1 then solved the MIP and its LP relaxation (numerically only).

**The returned assignment is exactly feasible.** All 5,263 equality rows hold with equality, and all 4,169 ≤ rows hold, in exact rational arithmetic. It has 3,301 ones and exact objective `10.289699734432698`, matching the reported source value.

**The LP relaxation is not tight.** Its optimum is `10.45677969…` against `10.28969973…`. So the solver's one-node `kOptimal` rests on presolve and root cuts, not on the relaxation alone, and no LP-dual certificate can prove optimality here. An exact proof would need an exact MIP solver or a verifiable cut and branch certificate.

**Rigorous ceiling.** I rationalized the LP row duals `y` (≤ rows clipped to `y ≥ 0`, the valid sign for this maximization) and computed all reduced costs exactly. By weak duality, every binary `x` satisfying the rows has

`cᵀx ≤ yᵀb + Σ_j max(0, rc_j) = cᵀx* + 0.16707995673637…`

This holds independently of the solver's correctness, and the bound is the same with duals rationalized at 10⁻¹² or 10⁻¹⁸. So **no assignment in this model improves the discount objective by more than 0.16708** at `a = 15108879/5000000000`. That bounds what a different solver run could ever find, though it does not show the true improvement is zero. The MPS objective coefficients are decimals of real-power prices; the bound concerns the model as written.

This agrees with the README's description of the run as numerical, not an exact global-optimality proof. It is an author-independent check, not acceptance, and κ is unchanged.
